findings.one_line: Terrain input and initialized-state wrapper interfaces are implemented and tracked but never driven by a probe and have no assertions; the audit does not check this.
The model.cpp size/hash drift is a classification error; the historical pin is correct and its 1864 B bytes are preserved in a tracked snapshot.
The vendor rule matches 33 WSL precheck receipts by filename text; none contains vendor bytes and all report found == [].
The pinned digest was never committed at the canonical path and is not a git object; re-verifiability rests on a single tracked snapshot, so the patch must fail closed when it is absent.
Three violations are Windows/WSL path-boundary artefacts for Linux-resident /root build and cold-rebuild libraries.
model_parameters.py and motor_efficiency_model.py hard-code the historical wrapper hash against the canonical path; not executed here, recorded only.

patch_plan.critical_constraint: The historical wrapper binding VALUE must remain 3f325678; only the bytes used to re-verify it may change. tools/audit_26_closure_readiness.py:884-889 cross-binds build staged hashes to lifecycle source hashes, so re-pointing the wrapper to today's source is self-contradictory.
